The published-surface export cannot carry a behavioural promise, so the capability ships a document that is structurally incomplete for the job it is offered for. Found by the dynograph-foundation trial, 2026-07-28.

Qualifies rather than overturns: skills stay served because a stale skill is silently wrong; commands are installed because a stale command is still correct, and the one way it could rot (naming a skill that no longer exists) is now a lint failure.

Corroboration, not conflict. The original reflow independently reached the same rule and wrote it as LESSON-01 of 00b-framework_selection.json — 'Do NOT default to UAF!' — with the reason that framework choice GATES which analyses are available, so a silent default chooses the analyses too. reflow2's Project.domain is that decision reduced to unread free text.

properties.note: THE BLOCKER, DRAWN AS AN EDGE RATHER THAN LEFT IN PROSE. This requirement wants the release procedure held as an ordered process, and cap:model-process is the Flow machinery that would hold it. It CANNOT yet: PART_OF_FLOW is declared Capability -> Flow and accepts nothing else, so a Flow's steps must be Capabilities, and a release chore is not a capability. Until that widens (a schema change, which moves the stamp), this requirement is unsatisfiable by the vocabulary it needs. Recorded as an edge deliberately — this session's own finding was that a prerequisite written into a description is a trigger nothing fires (cap:what-next sat parked after its condition cleared, because nothing watched the prose).

properties.evidence: It is that decision's 'the LLM speaks' half made explicit at the gap boundary; the human still decides and the graph still counts.
A bare gap question hands the user back the systems-engineering analysis that requirement exists to spare them; the recommendation is what makes it answerable without it.
Diagrams and mockups are binary or rendered content; the store is what makes them storable at all.
The graph already solved distribution by being a repo file plus merge-on-pull; blobs do not inherit that, which is why this requirement exists.
It is the distribution half of that requirement: a store nobody else can read delivers none of what it promised.
It completes that requirement rather than competing with it: session memory already models a transcript pointer and already names the machine-local-path flaw a content store fixes.
It is one answer to that requirement's problem: if a skill may never be loaded, the unskippable fraction has to live somewhere the agent cannot miss.
It is that requirement applied to the export door: a pointer that cannot resolve must be nameable by the person holding the document.
Without a measurement, whether that requirement is ever met is unknowable — the decay it names was found by asking an agent, not by any mechanism.
That requirement already arms the nudge on file-edit events and already names impact-check and link-artifacts; what is missing is shape-matching on top of it, not a new trigger.
Without a content store there is nowhere for the source documents to go.
It is that requirement's corpus whose sources are being kept; it extends corpus ingest rather than standing alone.
The store exists and is tested; this is the half that makes it usable by the agent and user that requirement is written for.

properties.note: How the schedule runs FORWARD rather than only recording what happened: readiness projections are TemporalFacts marked as forecast, so the epoch by which a technology clears its threshold is derivable. Answers this requirement's EXPECTED modality with evidence a reader can tell from measurement.

How readiness enters the satisfaction schedule: as an OBSERVATION on the enabling technology, with the gating threshold stated on what it gates and never defaulted. This is what lets the epoch a requirement is satisfied in be computed rather than declared, which is what this requirement asks for.

Which node type carries the re-injected payload depends on this decision: Snapshot has 14 live instances and already generalizes the P2-to-P3 Anchor, while Anchor has zero and is still advertised by describe_schema.

properties.description: Read requirements, functions and structure back out of a running system.
properties.name: Recover a design from an existing system

properties.description: `gap_id` keys an AGGREGATE gap — one per project, whose affected set is the population its rule ranges over — on the rule alone, so its id is stable while the design grows and an acknowledgement of it carries instead of being re-asked on every addition. Every other gap keeps hashing its affected nodes, because there a changed subject genuinely deserves a fresh judgement. The discriminator is an explicit exhaustive `GapSource::is_aggregate()`, so a new aggregate detector must decide rather than inherit. Paired with the `retired` reporting `reviewed_gaps` already had: a stable id is only safe because a review whose rule stops firing is still shown, rather than silently kept.
properties.name: A gap about the whole population is keyed on its rule, so a standing judgement carries

properties.description: Score function-to-structure allocation; cluster coupling.
properties.name: Analyse and propose allocation

properties.description: At an epoch or release, answers "what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to?" — every scheduled item returned as delivered, deferred (and where to), discontinued, or OUTSTANDING (still due here, not delivered, and nobody has said which of the previous two it is — the question to put to the user rather than default). Work scheduled after the baseline comes back separately, because a delta measured only against the plan cannot see the work that was not in it. `required` claims that did not land are reported as computed violations rather than slips — the scheduling face of a KPP. The baseline is the target's FIRST snapshot with every later one as the movement trail, so a total slip stays visible across repeated replans; where no snapshot exists the plan never moved and the live edges are the baseline. NOTHING IS STORED: the plan lives in the snapshots and delivery is computed from the golden thread, so writing the outcome down would create a second source of truth able to disagree with the first (`dec:arrival-delta`, `req:completion-computed`).
properties.name: What was planned against what arrived, computed and never stored

properties.description: A query surface on the graph's own time axis: what the design said at a given epoch, answered by the graph rather than by checking out an old export and reading it by hand. Anthony's acceptance tests, in his words (2026-07-30), are the target and the measure: which capabilities are due to be released in epoch 5, and what did we not achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10. The second is the harder half — it is a PLANNED-VERSUS-DELIVERED DELTA, computable only once an epoch has arrived, which is why this sits downstream of cap:planned-epochs. Reworded on Anthony's word 2026-07-30: the requirement previously described indexing git refs (the graph tracking where each snapshot lives), and that framing was retired when dec:where-plans-live settled that forward-looking plans describe graph content and stay in the graph — git keeps only the narrower job of pinning a version combination at an ARRIVED epoch. The original text is preserved at snap:epoch:planning-axis-intent:req:graph-indexes-snapshots. Approved for build by Anthony 2026-07-30.
properties.name: The graph answers as-of-epoch-n itself, without a git lookup

properties.description: The stopping rule for the tree cap:requirement-lineage now holds (Anthony, 2026-07-25). A requirement is ATOMIC when it cannot be split further without losing meaning and one person or team can build and test it. Without a termination condition a decomposition goes wrong in BOTH directions, and the second is the dangerous one because it looks like rigour: under-decomposed leaves a compound requirement nobody can test cleanly; OVER-decomposed turns requirements into task lists and code design (\"the system must lock the account after three failed attempts\" is atomic; \"the system must query the login_attempts column and check if the integer equals 3\" is not a requirement at all). THE SIGNALS SPLIT THE SAME WAY THE QUALITY CRITERIA DO (dec:three-party-checks), which is what makes this buildable rather than advice. CHEAP AND DETERMINISTIC — build first: NO CONJUNCTIONS, a literal scan of the statement for \"and\", \"or\", \"additionally\", which is a text check needing no model and catching the most common compound requirement; SINGLE OWNER, computable from the graph as whether the capabilities satisfying it allocate to ONE component, since a leaf whose delivery is spread across several parts is not one team's to own; SINGLE TESTING POINT, partly computable as whether it has exactly one check rather than several. SEMANTIC — the agent proposes, the human decides: ESTIMABLE, and OVER-DECOMPOSED, which is the same judgement as the minimally-constrained criterion in cap:requirement-quality seen from the other end — a requirement that dictates implementation and a requirement decomposed into implementation are the same error, and noticing that they are one thing means one detector can serve both. Pairs with cap:missing-sibling: that asks whether a family is missing a member, this asks whether its members are the right SIZE, and a family of uneven grain is a signal for both. PLANNED.
properties.name: Know when to stop decomposing — and when someone went too far

properties.description: From the same study: GitHub's server generates its instructions from the enabled toolsets and tells the agent in them to paginate in batches of 5-10 and pass minimal_output, and its result types carry field-selection enums whose comments name the heaviest fields. reflow2 has the same problem and lost to it twice in one session on 2026-07-25 — scan_nodes over 72 Decisions returned 96,000 characters and the harness had to spill it to a file before it could be read at all. The precedent for the shape is already in this design: BL-48/BL-49 gave propagate a bounded summary with the full dump behind full=true. This extends that to the readers that grew unbounded, with the rule that a cap is never silent: the page says how many nodes exist, how many came back, and how to get the rest.
properties.name: A read that would not fit answers with a bounded page and says what it left out

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the brainstorm skill + the /brainstorm command. Anthony's brother's original ask ("work through planning and idea realization before committing concepts to graph... an agent-assisted thinking process"), reframed by Anthony into what it actually is: not a staging gate but a KIND of record. Ideas enter the graph immediately as `proposed` Decisions named as open questions, with the options in the decision text and the honest counter-argument beside each; nothing waits outside in a buffer where it could be forgotten, and nothing is claimed as intent. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT WORK WAS ALREADY THERE, found while building: detect_gaps raises undecided_decision_point ONLY on a proposed Decision with two or more REGISTERED alternatives, so a Decision whose options live in prose is silent by construction — and the nudge to choose arrives exactly when register_alternative turns an option into a fork with a design behind it. The loop stays quiet while someone thinks, and speaks the moment the ideas stop being ideas. No label, no schema change, no upgrade doc. THE GUARDS, all prose because none is machine-checkable: never create Requirements or Capabilities from a brainstorm (promotion is a separate step needing the user's word); never argue an idea down in conversation — record the objection beside it, because an idea killed in dialogue loses its reasoning; never run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes, which would ask the user to firm up exactly what they left soft; and never promote the last idea standing, since one remaining idea nobody chose is still an idea nobody chose. set_decision_status to `proposed` is mandatory, because add_decision defaults to `accepted` and would assert a settlement that never happened. Ends as a PROMOTION step, not a commit step: chosen ideas go through capture-intent, the rest stay recorded as considered rather than deleted (req:roads-not-taken). The one honest weakness is readability — a person scanning the decision list cannot tell a musing from a choice without reading the prose, which is what the open vocabulary question in dec:exploratory-staging is now reduced to.
properties.name: Work an idea through without committing to it, on the record

properties.description: Sum contributions along the thread; refuse a total it cannot honestly compute.
properties.name: Roll up a budget against a constraint

properties.description: Bulk forms for every tool BL-153's surface measurement caught calling itself: create_nodes, create_edges, set_artifact_checksums, acknowledge_gaps, gaps_to_prompts. 52.9% of all tool-to-tool transitions across 46 sessions and 6,095 calls were self-loops; these answer set_artifact_checksum 244, create_node 112, contains 109, acknowledge_gap 90, gap_to_prompt 83, contain_component 77 and satisfies 74. create_edges is ONE tool rather than six because contains/contain_component/satisfies/allocate/realizes are thin wrappers that only fill in the endpoint types, and BL-155's 40-never-called count makes near-identical tools a cost. Every form is all-or-nothing WITH per-item findings, and every form that records a judgement keeps that judgement per item.
properties.name: One call where the surface measured N

properties.description: Snapshot prior state at an epoch, then edit — axis Z.
properties.name: Record a change

properties.description: Anthony's B+K / B-K case, 2026-07-25: the project does A, B, C and D, and the ask is to make B do something more (or less). Distinct from cap:onboarding (BL-101), which answers where a NEW thing belongs — this answers where an EXISTING thing gets extended or narrowed, and the difference matters because the answer is shaped by what B already touches rather than by where a gap is. Mostly composition of machinery that exists and has never been aimed at this question: search_design maps the user's words onto B; propagate_from gives the blast radius of touching it; the Decision layer says what already governs B and must not be casually contradicted; cap:requirement-lineage would say whether B is a decomposed child (so the parent's other children are siblings that may need the same change) or carries derived requirements that the extension might invalidate. THE SIMPLIFICATION DIRECTION IS THE INTERESTING HALF and is not symmetric with extension: removing capability from B means asking what still depends on it, which is propagate run the other way, and then whether any requirement is left unsatisfied by the removal — a question retire-from-design already forces for a whole node but nobody asks for a partial reduction. Removing is where designs are damaged quietly, because the thing that breaks is usually not the thing being edited. PLANNED.
properties.name: Show where to extend or simplify a feature that already exists

properties.description: Derive a Keep a Changelog-shaped draft (keepachangelog.com, Anthony's pointer 2026-07-28) between any two Releases or Epochs, from what the graph already records: the INCLUDES delta between two Release manifests (what appeared, what left) plus the dated ChangeEvents and drift accepts between their epochs, classified into the KaC buckets — Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed — mapped from the vocabulary the graph already carries (new nodes and link_artifact baselines -> Added; design_updated accepts and amended statements -> Changed; retire-from-design with history -> Deprecated/Removed; design_holds accepts with change_type test_failure_fix -> Fixed). The [Unreleased] section is the standing case: everything dated after the last deployed Release — which makes 'what would this increment's changelog say?' answerable BEFORE cutting it, the capability-increment sibling of what-next. Two KaC principles carried over as constraints: changelogs are FOR HUMANS, curated — this emits a DRAFT a person edits, never a commit-log dump (KaC names raw logs an antipattern; dec:report-dont-judge is the same rule here) — and every entry says what a CONSUMER does about it, which the graph cannot know alone. Kin to cap:compare-designs (two as-designed records); this compares two moments of ONE design and renders the difference in the format industry already reads. DIRECTIONALITY, Anthony's formulation 2026-07-28, which is the load-bearing claim: 'our delta is a graph/machine version of a human changelog; the agent could derive the human changelog from the graph delta. Basically: graph delta --via_agent--> human changelog.' The graph delta is the primary, machine-readable record; the human changelog is a derived rendering, and never the other way around -- when the two disagree, the graph is what is interrogated and the changelog is what gets regenerated.
properties.name: A changelog is a derivable view of the graph's own delta

properties.description: Every claim records a seat — machine:pid:mint, minted once per process with zero coordination — defaulting to the session making it, overridable with a durable handle (a fleet worker name). claim_report then COMPUTES liveness by asking the operating system whether that process still exists: nothing writes "I am alive", so nothing can be stale. A claim whose session exited is reported `gone`, listed in `stale` with its note intact, and EXCLUDED from overlaps, because a collision with nobody is not a collision and reporting it as one is how an advisory report starts lying. A claim from another machine, or from before seats were recorded, is `unknown` and still counts as a possible collision — reading it as free would invite somebody to take work that is actively being done.
properties.name: A claim names the session that made it, and a claim nobody is working says so

properties.description: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it (BL-44). BUILT 2026-07-25 as claims.rs, exposed as claim_region / release_claim / claim_report (96 tools). A new CLAIMS edge, Contributor → any node, carrying depth / claimed_at / note. THE SHAPE IS SET BY dec:multi-writer-architecture, and every part of it follows from having no server. A CLAIM IS NOT A LOCK. Nothing in the module refuses a write and nothing anywhere consults a claim before allowing one; a second writer who ignores a claim gets a correct three-way merge exactly as if it did not exist. That is pinned by a test rather than promised in a comment, because a claims layer that READS like locking is worse than none — it invites reliance on a guarantee it cannot make. THE REGION IS COMPUTED, never stored: a claim holds a seed and a depth, and the membership is derived through the same traversal propagate_from uses, so it follows the design as the design changes instead of freezing a list that silently goes wrong the moment someone adds an edge (pinned: new work inside a claimed area is covered without re-claiming). OVERLAP IS REPORTED, NEVER PREVENTED. Two people may claim the same ground and both claims stand; claim_report names the shared nodes and ranks collisions by size, because a two-node brush and a forty-node collision should not read alike. Two claims by the SAME person are not a collision — reporting them would train people to ignore the list, which is how a signal dies. The advisory limit ships IN the payload, not only in the docs, since whoever reads it over the wire never sees the docs. CLAIMS is deliberately NOT a traceability edge, like AUTHORED_BY: who is working on something is coordination, not design structure, and propagating it would drag people into every blast radius (pinned by a test). 9 tests. Schema change: edge types 54 → 55.
properties.name: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it

properties.description: Load N alternative design exports (branch-by-file) and report each branch on the same measures — graph_report snapshot (nodes, open gaps, allocation health, verification coverage) side by side — plus each branch's structural divergence from a named baseline (compare_designs). Alternatives comparable on measures, not advocacy. BL-70 v1; the collapse (merge winner + retire losers) reuses BL-80. Rung 2 wires the decision point.
properties.name: Compare parallel alternatives on the same measures (AoA)

properties.description: Diff two export documents (or the live graph against one) into added / removed / changed relative to a named base, banded into design content vs bookkeeping, property-level on changes.
properties.name: Compare two as-designed records

properties.description:
`Interface.designation` carries the boundary's external ROLE — `published` (offers), `required` (needs one from outside), `both`, or `internal` — and `pair_designs` matches COMPLEMENTS across two designs: published/both against required/both, never like with like. The `required` half did not exist before 2026-07-30, which is why a design could say what it offered but not what it needed in any form another design could be matched against.

Two boundaries pair when their names match fuzzily (reusing ingest's two-band resolution rather than a second matcher) AND they agree on `medium`, `transport_security` and `auth`. Five outcomes: paired, CONFLICTS (names match, axes refuse — reported with every refusing axis), unmet needs, dead surface, and duplicate providers. Uncertain names are candidates to ask about, never actions. Boundaries with no role are counted and named, because `internal` is the default and cannot distinguish a deliberate choice from an unlabelled one. Produces the pairs `seam_report` previously had to be handed by a person.
properties.name: Two designs pair by complementary role, so the seam is computed rather than hand-wired

properties.description: compose_and_analyse imports another design alongside this one and runs reflow2's ORDINARY checks — detect_gaps and detect_defects — over the combined whole, so seam problems arrive as the gaps they already are rather than needing a bespoke comparator. Anthony's mechanism, and better than the comparison the requirement first implied: make the existing computation SEE more rather than write a new one. WHY IT IS NOT import_graph: that writes every node under its ORIGINAL id with upsert semantics, because it exists to layer an export onto the design it came from — point it at a DIFFERENT design and the dependency's cmp:store silently overwrites the consumer's, which is corruption with no error. Ids are therefore namespaced to {namespace}::{id}, edges rewritten with them, and an empty namespace is REFUSED rather than allowed to collide by omission. NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO EITHER DESIGN: the combined graph is built in memory and thrown away, following the ingest handshake's prepare-round precedent. That disposes of both hazards the requirement named — an export of yours can never start carrying theirs, and there is no residue to clean up — and it is pinned by a test asserting your export's content_hash is byte-identical afterwards. FINDINGS ARE ATTRIBUTED ours / theirs / seam, because a consumer shown its dependency's internal gaps as if they were its own will switch the feature off, and rightly. The seam bucket is the point: findings neither design could have produced alone. Sits alongside the two composition mechanisms that already existed without replacing either — mirror_surface takes the published surface only and keeps it foreign, merge_designs reconciles two versions of the SAME design — and it does not overturn dec:nested-graphs, since ownership and release stay separate; this is a third, analysis-only composition.
properties.name: Analyse two designs together without merging them

properties.description:
Content hash → readable name → what references it, so a design that points at stored content can say what it does NOT itself carry. `missing` names content the graph references and this checkout lacks — the case someone handed the export alone hits, where a diagram that will not open becomes a named finding instead of a silent absence. `orphaned` is the reverse: bytes stored and referenced by nothing, which is how a store grows without anyone deciding to (and the reason `dec:where-content-lives` left repo growth deliberately open).

DERIVED, NEVER STORED, and that is the design rather than an optimisation. The manifest is computed from the graph plus a directory listing; a manifest kept as its own record would be a second source of truth about what the design references and would drift the first time someone updated one and not the other. Rendering it to a committed markdown file is a PROJECTION — the same relationship `dec:views-are-projections` already sets for every other view.

THE READABLE NAME IS THE FRAGMENT'S `title`, not a filename stored beside the hash. The graph already requires a title, so there is no second place for names to live and nothing to disagree with the design about what a thing is called. `referenced_by` carries the Fragment AND what it annotates or yielded, so "what is this picture for?" is answerable from the manifest without opening anything.

A LOCATOR AFTER THE HASH TRAVELS VERBATIM and is never parsed (`dec:agent-navigates-content`) — `sha256:…#L412-L440` resolves to the same blob and reports `L412-L440` untouched. A `content_ref` holding a plain PATH from before the store existed is not treated as content at all, so legacy references do not read as missing blobs.

Needed a FOURTH store function, `list` — named rather than slipped in, because `dec:content-store-implementation` argued for three. That argument was about `object_store`'s path/prefix/pagination semantics, which immutable content addressing does not need; enumerating a flat set of addresses is a different thing, and orphan detection is impossible without it. `list` skips anything whose name is not a hash, so a stranded temp file or the committed manifest is never mistaken for content.

Paired with `.gitattributes` marking the blob directory `binary` — which stops git attempting diffs it cannot produce and, the part that matters, stops line-ending conversion silently corrupting a PNG on a CRLF checkout. REALIZED; `ver:content-manifest` passing, served as `content_manifest`.
properties.name: Say what content the design depends on, in names a person can read

properties.description:
A content-addressed store for what the graph cannot hold inline — session transcripts, mermaid diagrams, HTML mockups, user-supplied drawings and photographs, and the source documents a corpus was extracted from. The graph records a CONTENT HASH; the bytes live in the store; an unresolvable pointer fails loud and names itself rather than rendering a design quietly missing its pictures.

HAND-ROLLED AND SYNCHRONOUS, IN `reflow2-core` (`dec:content-store-implementation`). `put` / `get` / `exists` over `sha2` and `std::fs`. Zero new crates in the core, no async runtime. `object_store` was measured and recorded as the documented UPGRADE PATH rather than adopted: 36 crates new to reflow2, ~24 of them URL/ICU machinery a local store never calls, buying a feature set — paths, prefixes, listing, multipart, conditional writes — that immutable content addressing does not have.

REACHABLE FROM A SESSION as `content_put` / `content_get` / `content_exists` (`req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session`). That requirement exists because this capability was first marked `realized` while NOTHING COULD CALL IT — complete in the core, tested, carrying a passing check, and unreachable by every agent and person who would use it. Content arrives as `text` or `base64` (JSON carries no raw bytes), exactly one, and the store's root comes from `--content-path` rather than being derived from `--graph-path`, because the graph lives under a gitignored directory and blobs are COMMITTED so they travel with the design.

FOUR REFUSALS, which is where this earns its keep — each pinned by a test, two mutation-checked. `get` VERIFIES bytes against the hash they are stored under and refuses a mismatch: a content hash nobody checks is only a filename. A malformed hash is refused BEFORE it reaches the filesystem, since a hash is interpolated into a path. Passing both `text` and `base64` is refused rather than resolved by picking one. And a server with no store configured says so instead of inventing a directory — where blobs live is a decision about the consumer's repo.

Writes are temp-then-rename, so a process that dies mid-write leaves nothing or a whole blob, and a stranded temp file is unreachable as content because its name is not a hash. Reading INTO stored content is not this capability's job and never becomes one — the agent navigates, the graph records an opaque locator reflow2 never parses (`dec:agent-navigates-content`). What belongs here versus natively in the repo is `dec:what-lives-where`. REALIZED; `ver:content-store` and `ver:content-surface` passing.
properties.name: Store bytes beside the design and point at them by content hash

properties.description: Take a directory of written specifications and produce one coherent design from the whole corpus, keeping each claim's provenance Fragment pointing back at its source document. Extends single-document extraction, which already works, with the two things a corpus needs and a file does not: a folder driver, and identity resolution ACROSS documents so the same thing named in many specs converges on one node. The primitive for that convergence already exists — every node type declares its own resolution strategy and threshold in the schema — so this is wiring an existing mechanism at batch scale rather than inventing one. Bound by dec:ask-not-repair: suspected duplicates are asked, never silently merged, which at corpus scale means the asking must be batched or the feature is unusable. PLANNED — BL-97.
properties.name: Ingest a folder of specifications as one design

properties.description: Compare the design against an agent-supplied sweep of the real system and report the regions no node claims, ranked by mass, so the largest silences surface first. The sibling of reconcile_artifacts (design vs reality) and its opposite in subject: reconcile asks "has what I know about changed?", coverage asks "what is there that I have never been told about?". THE FAILURE IT CLOSES: every other detector reasons about nodes already in the graph, so a design covering 30% of a system reported the same `0 open gaps` as one covering all of it — and merge.rs plus alternatives.rs, 1,886 lines shipped in v0.10.0, sat unmodelled in reflow2's own repository for two days with nothing firing. reflow2 performs NO FILE I/O — the agent sweeps and supplies the paths, exactly as reconcile does with checksums, so the answer is only ever as wide as the sweep. Measures CLAIMED REGIONS, never a file-count ratio, because the modelling doctrine mandates one artifact per meaningful unit and one opaque component for a vendored mass; counting files would punish correct coarse modelling, so an artifact whose location is a directory claims everything beneath it. Unclaimed paths roll up to the shallowest wholly-unclaimed directory, or a vendored tree arrives as 900 findings nobody reads. Excluded regions are named as excluded with the rule that excluded them, never silently dropped. Reports the sweep's date so stale coverage is never read as current, and names registered locations the sweep never mentioned so "my sweep was narrower than the design" is distinguishable from "the file is gone". Reports, never scores, never blocks (dec:report-dont-judge). BUILT 2026-07-27 as coverage_report on the core and the MCP surface, and wired into the adopt skill's Phase 4 so a thin pass is measured rather than felt. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, recorded rather than half-done: the sweep is NOT PERSISTED, so detect_gaps cannot raise coverage from graph state the way unresolved_drift is raised from a recorded DriftEvent. That needs a node to record a sweep in (a schema change) and a decision about how stale a recorded sweep may be before its claim expires (the cap:freshness precedent). Until then coverage is something a person asks for, and adopt ends by asking.
properties.name: Say what the design has never heard of

properties.description: BL-141(a). Every circular_dependency finding now states its basis: the Interfaces any hop was collapsed out of, whether ANY hop is backed by a real DEPENDS_ON edge, and whether every Interface involved is a library/data medium — something read or linked against rather than called across at run time. dependency_pairs collapses `c CONSUMES i` + `p PROVIDES i` into a direct pair, which is correct for detection and discards the one datum a reader needs to tell a coarse interface model from a tangled call graph; the medium is now kept beside the pair instead of thrown away. A REPORT, never a verdict (dec:report-dont-judge): reflow2 cannot know whether one Interface node is standing for two contracts, so it names what it walked and leaves the judgement to the reader — the BL-114 fix shape applied to this detector. Detection semantics are UNCHANGED: the same cycles are found, with the same severity. Whether a foundation-medium contract loop should count as a dependency cycle at all is BL-141(b), still open.
properties.name: A dependency cycle says which edge kinds it walked, and through which contracts

properties.description: A proposed Decision is a decision point: register alternatives under it as lightweight Artifact pointers (branch-by-file, each naming its export), GOVERNED_BY the Decision and CONTRADICTS their siblings — the fork held open. Refuses registering under a settled decision. Collapse chooses a winner: the Decision moves to accepted, losers are superseded (OBSOLETES, retired on the record not deleted), and the outcome + rationale are written into the Decision's own alternatives field. The teeth: the undecided_decision_point DETECT gap surfaces a proposed Decision with >=2 alternatives as an open fork ('which do you choose?'), anchored so it clears on collapse. The winner's content-merge reuses apply_merge. BL-70 rung 2; ops set_decision_status, register_alternative, alternatives_for, collapse_decision.
properties.name: Hold and collapse a decision point (forkable alternatives)

properties.description: On any open failure, serve a handshake plus exactly one tool (reflow2_unavailable) whose name is the diagnosis, with the translated reason in the server instructions, the remedies in the tool payload, and an explicit do-not-conclude-reflow2-is-missing.
properties.name: The server explains its own absence instead of vanishing

properties.description: The pull for the graph: after git pull, bring this machine's live store and the working tree back into one coherent state, orchestrating what already exists. Layer 1 syncs the record — find the base (the newest export in git history both lines share), snapshot the live store (--export-snapshot works while the long-running session's server holds the lock), then fast-forward (import_graph upsert-layering, built for layering a design onto itself) when the store never moved, or the file-pure three-way (--merge to see conflicts, decide, --merge-apply) when both moved, then import the merged document and re-export straight onto the committed file so the lineage chain links. Layer 2 reconciles the code — commits in the pull that never updated the graph: reconcile_artifacts and coverage_report over the paths git names since the base, each finding walked to a two-sided answer (set_artifact_checksum / link_artifact / retire), a mini adopt pass where intent must be recovered. REVIEW MODE (req:pr-is-a-delta): the same layer-2 reading pointed at a candidate change instead of a landed one — checkout or worktree of the PR, drifted-artifact set, propagate to the capabilities/interfaces/requirements they realize, touched published or consumed interfaces named explicitly — and strictly read-only: no accepts, no writes, a report; the write half runs only when the change lands. Precedent: the 'Live-store catch-up' ChangeEvents of 2026-07-23 did layer 1 by hand; this packages that discipline. reflow2 performs no file I/O — git evidence is swept and supplied by the agent. CHANGELOG, both directions (Anthony, 2026-07-28, via keepachangelog.com): as INPUT, layer 2's intent recovery harvests the project's own changelog for the pulled range first — a changelog is the delta a human already curated, better evidence of intent than any diff — and as OUTPUT, the delta report is changelog-shaped (the KaC buckets via cap:changelog-view), so what the reconcile found reads like a document industry already knows how to read.
properties.name: Delta reconcile: present what changed since the graph last matched

properties.description: Derive a requirement's delivery state from the golden thread rather than reading a hand-set field. BUILT 2026-07-24 as `delivery_coverage()` in report.rs, surfaced on graph_report as `delivery` and as a line in the Markdown view. A requirement is DELIVERED when something satisfies it AND that capability is realized AND currently carries a passing check, at its own or component granularity. Two properties are load-bearing and both are pinned by tests. FIRST, it goes BACKWARDS: because capability_verification only reports Verified/ComponentVerified for checks that pass (dec:passing-is-verified), a requirement stops being delivered the moment its check starts failing, with nobody editing anything — a derivation that can only ratchet up is a stored claim with extra steps. SECOND, inference is not evidence: a requirement whose own provenance is `inferred` was read back out of the code implementing it, so its satisfaction is a tautology; those are counted apart as `inferred_only` rather than silently dropped, because otherwise a brownfield adopt would report itself fully delivered on arrival. Dropped requirements are excluded from the denominator — abandoning a need is not failing to deliver it. FIRST REAL ANSWER, against reflow2's own design the day it was built: 20 of 30 requirements delivered, 29 satisfied — a question that was flatly unanswerable an hour earlier, when zero requirements carried `met`. STILL TO DO from the original scope, deliberately not built here: distinguishing SUPERSEDED from DROPPED from EVOLVED, and surfacing MET-BUT-REGRESSED as a TemporalFact with VALID_TO. The headline number came first because it is what makes the rest legible.
properties.name: Compute what is delivered, and expose the requirement lifecycle that is currently unused

properties.description: One call packages a release: every Artifact and every Component the design holds becomes an INCLUDES edge, with each artifact's current checksum frozen as shipped. It is the bulk form of release_includes, which was the single largest line item in reflow2's entire recorded usage (BL-153: 1008 calls across 7 sessions, 988 of them consecutive, ~144 per release cut) — all of it typing out something the graph already knew, and the rule AGENTS.md already states: a release "must list every component that goes out, not a hand-maintained roll-call". Nothing is written unless applied, re-running never rewrites a frozen checksum, an exclusion that names nothing is refused, and the artifacts whose entry cannot say WHAT shipped are reported by name. Measured on reflow2's own design: 160 edges in one call.
properties.name: A release's manifest is derived from the design, not typed out

properties.description: A dependency declaration records the source, the version a design MEANS to depend on, the parts taken and the build switches forwarded by name; `reconcile_dependencies` compares that against what the build actually resolves and reports both opposite failures — the build taking something nothing declares, and a declaration the build no longer takes. `dependency_manifest` emits `reflow2.toml`, stamped with which reflow2 produced it. Declaring nothing reads as "nobody has said", never as "depends on nothing".
properties.name: Declare which version of another design you depend on, and check it against the build

properties.description: An id is established on first open and read on every one after, from <graph-path>.id.json — a sibling of the store, because the id namespaces every stored key and so must be known before the design can be read. Minted with zero coordination (creation nanosecond + process + absolute path through fnv1a, no dependency added); the friendly label is a changeable layer on top and never load-bearing. An unreadable identity is REFUSED, never defaulted, because defaulting opens a different design at the same path and reports nothing wrong. THE MIGRATION IS THE FEATURE: a store that already holds a design under the old shared id adopts that id forever, which is what keeps every existing export, chain link and committed record valid — graph_id is inside the export's content hash. Served as design_identity (read, or rename via label).
properties.name: A design is given a name nobody negotiates for, and keeps it

properties.description: Find what the design has not decided yet, ranked.
properties.name: Detect gaps

properties.description: Assess nodes on dimensions and detect decline.
properties.name: Track quality over time

properties.description: Say which way the design and the build have diverged, not merely that they have. Anthony's founding problem, observed in the field 2026-07-24 (reflow2 on storyflow: the docs "consistently understate what's built") and the failure the predecessor died of. BUILT 2026-07-25, pieces 1 and 2 of 3. HOW: ObservedArtifact gains an optional `realizes` — what the caller observed the file actually implementing. Core compares that against the recorded REALIZES edges, which keeps the no-file-IO contract intact (the agent observes, the core computes) and yields both halves at once. DIRECTION: more observed than recorded is Understated, less is Overstated, each-having-what-the-other-lacks is Diverged. MEANING: the finding carries `unrecorded` and `unbuilt` — the specific design nodes involved — and the message names them, which is the answer to "what does the design now claim wrongly?" that a checksum could never give. Without it, accepting drift means asking someone to go find the delta themselves, and that is the labour that does not happen under load. FOUR JUDGEMENTS WORTH KNOWING. (a) Direction is assessed INDEPENDENTLY of the checksum: a design can be wrong from the day it was written, and tying this to checksum_change would miss the long-lived untouched files where understatement accumulates. (b) Overstatement outranks understatement and plain change, because a design claiming something absent is what someone will plan against — understatement is a record that is behind, overstatement is a record that is wrong. (c) `realizes: None` means not assessed and is never read as agreement, so no existing caller silently starts asserting alignment it never checked. (d) Mapped onto the EXISTING schema drift_types (understated records as undocumented_addition, which is what it is one level down; overstated as spec_mismatch) rather than adding two enum values — a schema change costs a minor bump, an upgrade doc and real pain for anyone on an older stamp (BL-94), and buys nothing here. NOT BUILT: piece 3, write-back to the source documents a design was adopted from. The graph can now be brought up to date; the markdown people actually read still cannot.
properties.name: Say which way the design and the build have diverged, and bring the design back up

properties.description: A check now records WHERE it was carried out (PERFORMED_IN → Environment), and Environment.env_type gains `simulation`. evidence_report then answers, per capability, which environments its PASSING checks were performed in and whether every one of them was a simulation. THE REASON THIS IS THE FIRST RUNG of req:design-the-simulator: the argument for simulating first is that issues are cheap to fix there and expensive in the field, and that argument only holds if somebody can still tell the two apart afterwards — until 2026-07-27 reflow2 could not, because a rig run and a production run were both simply `passing`. REPORTS, NEVER RANKS (Anthony's call, dec:report-dont-judge): it says `proven only in simulation`, which env_type alone can defend, and refuses to assert that lab beats staging beats field — which of those counts as more real is domain-specific, and an ordering that is wrong somewhere gets worked around rather than corrected (BL-42's lesson). SILENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF THE FIELD: a passing check naming no environment is counted as UNPLACED, never assumed real, because the flattering reading is the dangerous one. A capability with nothing passing is absent from the report entirely — that is unverified_capability's question, not this one's. THE SIMULATOR AS A DESIGNED THING is deliberately NOT built here: the requirement's other half wants the simulator to have its own requirements and fidelity claims, and nothing yet expresses what a given rig stands in for. Recorded rather than half-built, and no vocabulary was added for it, because a declared edge no computation reads is the trap this project has now hit five times.
properties.name: Tell proof against a model from proof against reality

properties.description: The INPUT axis of the evidence-quality family (BL-126). Records on each VERIFIES edge the parameters a check SWEPT and the ones it PINNED, and reports per capability which parameters every passing check pinned and none swept — the state BL-126 names as '31 checks, all at one value'. Reported as a FACT on the evidence report beside WHERE the evidence came from, never as a gap: a pinned parameter is a standing property of the evidence, and a detector that fired on every check with a fixed seed would punish correct work, which is the BL-23 failure the gap workflow exists to prevent. Checks stating no scope at all are counted as unscoped and reported, never read as full coverage. Deliberately does NOT execute, fuzz or vary anything (dec:loop-status-state-not-history, 'looking is not writing'): it makes the narrowness of the evidence visible and leaves the varying to whoever runs the tests.
properties.name: Say what a check held fixed and what it varied, per claim

properties.description: The plain-language entry surface: what reflow2 physically is, how it runs on the reader's own machine, where the agent instructions go, and a few concrete uses — before any doctrine. Realized by documentation artifacts (README, the getting-started material, diagrams) rather than by code, which is why it is a capability with no module: what satisfies it is prose and pictures. PLANNED — BL-102. Deliberately left unallocated at capture: which part of the project owns its own explanation is a real question, not an obvious one, and inventing an owner would be a renderer fill-in of the kind dec:views-are-projections forbids.
properties.name: Explain itself to someone who has not been convinced yet

properties.description: Keep every Decision's unchosen options as forkable siblings; re-open a past decision at its epoch and take a different branch, with the alternative's consequence design computed by replay (propagate/compare) rather than pre-stored. Selection of which fork to expand follows the reward signal — defects and field trials — not the whole tree; the human does the credit assignment. The navigation layer of reflow2-as-decision-MDP, unifying BL-70 (branches), BL-80 (merge, how a road comes home) and BL-44 (claims). DESIGNED 2026-07-24: the fork point is a coordinate, decision → AT_EPOCH → epoch.checksum → the committed export (dec:fork-point-address), so no ref/DAG layer is needed; re-opening mints a superseding Decision rather than un-accepting the original (dec:reopen-supersedes); the epoch chain the whole thing addresses is backfilled from real release tags (dec:temporal-backfill-from-releases). STILL TO BUILD: the read-only fork_point operation that resolves a Decision to its epoch, checksum and governed blast radius, and reports what has changed since — the base a three-way merge then takes to bring a road home.
properties.name: Hold and re-fork a decision's unchosen alternatives

properties.description: Distinguish a design that matches reality from one nobody has checked.
properties.name: Say when a claim was last confirmed

properties.description:
When a choice is put to the user, the agent's reading travels with it: the recommended answer, why, and the condition under which the other option wins. The decision stays with the user — no status moves on a recommendation alone.

THE SHAPE IS PART OF THE CAPABILITY, added 2026-07-31 on Anthony's word after the pattern was used on him for the five standing gaps and he asked for it to be CEMENTED rather than repeated. Three separable obligations: the options are SELECTABLE rather than buried in prose, so the user picks instead of composing a reply; the RECOMMENDATION IS FIRST and marked as such, because an unordered menu makes the user infer which one the agent favours — the very analysis req:no-se-knowledge exists to spare them; and EVERY option carries its consequence, including the ones not recommended, because a list of bare labels looks complete while withholding what each choice costs.

THE LANGUAGE IS THE USER'S, NOT ENGLISH. Anthony's words: "with agents able to understand multiple languages, the 'simple english' should be 'simple whatever_language_user_is_writing_in'." The plainness obligation is about REGISTER — no jargon, no node ids, short sentences — and register is language-independent. cap:surface already says "in the user's WORDS"; this makes the wider reading explicit so nobody implements it as an English-only rule. Every English phrasing in the design notes is an example of the register, never a specification of the language.

DELIBERATELY A NEW CAPABILITY RATHER THAN AN EXTENSION OF `cap:surface`. That capability is `verified` for what it does — turning a gap into a question in the user's words — and widening it would repeat the BL-106 defect exactly: a capability is not one behaviour, so adding a second one behind an existing passing check makes the check cover less than it appears to. New behaviour, new capability, its own check. The same argument is why the shape and language obligations land HERE and not back inside cap:surface.

WHAT IS TESTABLE AND WHAT IS NOT, stated so the check does not overclaim: whether a recommendation is GOOD, and whether the language was correctly matched, are semantic judgements and stay evidenced by trials (docs/sharpening.md — deliberately no LLM evals in CI). What IS mechanically checkable is the contract: that the skill states all three shape obligations and the counterweight rule; that it states the language rule in language-independent terms; that no served text hardcodes English as the answer language; and that no requirement status, decision status or gap acknowledgement is ever written in the same act as a recommendation.

SCOPE WIDENED BY THE SAME REQUEST: this began as a rule about GAPS, and Anthony's framing — "the decisions I need to make" — is broader. Read as covering any point where the agent puts a CHOICE to the user, not only where detect_gaps produced it. Whether that widening deserves its own capability is left open in req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading rather than assumed here.

Governed by `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`. PLANNED, scheduled `expected` for rel:v0210.
properties.name: A question arrives as options the user can pick, recommendation first, in their own language

properties.description: Seed a project, its requirements and capabilities, refusing to clobber an existing graph.
properties.name: Bootstrap a design from a brief

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as `reflow2-mcp --merge-driver %O %A %B`, plus the `.gitattributes` entry and the parallel-work skill. THE PROBLEM IT ANSWERS, from Anthony's own doubt while brainstorming the isolation ideas: claiming a cluster of nodes says nothing about the REPOSITORY, so two people working entirely separate parts of one design still collide in git — the export is a single large JSON document and git merges it by lines, a unit that means nothing to a graph. The merge itself already existed (BL-80: per node, per property, against the common ancestor, conflicts minted as Questions with deterministic ids); what was missing was one adapter so git calls it. Git's contract followed exactly: exit 0 means merged with the result in %A, non-zero means conflicts remain and the path stays unmerged for a human. A clean merge is written and succeeds; a real both-sides conflict exits non-zero WITHOUT touching %A and prints each conflict id, its question and the `--merge-apply` command that finishes the job — because a driver that fails silently at a git prompt is how someone reaches for `--ours` and deletes a node the other person wrote. NOTHING IS AUTO-DECIDED: the driver applies only what one-sided changes make derivable, running the same resolve_merge the apply path uses so it can take no shortcut of its own. Tested by GIT, not by a home-grown client (tools/test_merge_driver.py, 4 cases on real branches): disjoint edits merge with no human, both-sides conflicts leave the path unmerged and name themselves, additions from both sides both survive, and an unconfigured clone degrades to git's text merge instead of failing — because .gitattributes travels with the repo and the driver definition cannot.
properties.name: Be git's merge driver for the design, so disjoint work merges itself

properties.description: `set_project_mode` chooses a project's `mode` after genesis and can change it later, so the one default that actually alters behaviour stops being asserted by omission. The mode gates exactly one thing — `apply_heal` applies structural repairs in `flexible` and only proposes them in `rigid` — and the schema description now says that rather than the older, broader "design is the source of truth", which promised a breadth the code does not implement. An unknown mode is refused by schema validation and leaves the previous choice intact.
properties.name: The governance mode is a choice a project makes and can revisit

properties.description: Propose content-free structural fixes, then apply atomically.
properties.name: Repair structure

properties.description: Find missing intermediates and level mismatches — axis Y.
properties.name: Check decomposition levels

properties.description: The INDEPENDENCE axis of the evidence-quality family (BL-136). Reads the CALIBRATED_AGAINST edges recording what a value was derived from, and marks any VERIFIES edge whose Verification IS, or PRODUCES, evidence its own target was calibrated against as CONSUMED — a fit, not a test. Consumed checks are excluded from the count of independent evidence, so a capability whose only passing checks are consumed reports as not independently verified. Structural by construction and not analytic: BL-136's originating project built four independent internal diagnostics and none could have found the defect, because no check inside a design can establish its own independence — only the outside source could. So this records and reports the relation rather than attempting to detect circularity from the evidence itself.
properties.name: Refuse to let evidence a value was fitted to count as its validation

properties.description: Multi-pass LLM extraction with provenance.
properties.name: Extract a design from freeform text

properties.description: When a project owns no instruction file at all — the ordinary state of a repo that has never been agent-worked, and therefore of an adopt target — the installer CREATES the primary-harness convention carrying a pointer to the kit's own file, instead of only appending to files that already exist. Narrow on purpose: a project that already owns any instruction convention gets a line appended to it and nothing invented, and the created file stays a pointer rather than a second home for instructions.
properties.name: The install lands where the agent will actually read it

properties.description: Interface gains the properties two systems actually have to agree on, structured so a computation can compare them: paradigm (synchronous / asynchronous / streaming / batch), payload_format, payload_schema, endpoint, operations, auth, transport_security and error_model, set through set_interface_spec. Before this, Interface carried the technology (medium) and its published/internal designation, and everything else went into one free-text `spec` string — so two designs could be linked and reflow2 still could not say they disagreed, because prose cannot be compared. EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL AND OMITTING ONE LEAVES IT ALONE, so a spec can be filled in over time and by different people without one person's entry erasing another's — pinned by a test. UNSET READS AS `unspecified`, NEVER A FLATTERING DEFAULT: silence about authentication must not read as `none`, which would tell a consumer the contract is open when nobody has said anything at all. An invented enum value is refused rather than stored, because the vocabulary is what two designs get compared in and a typo'd auth scheme would make a sound seam look mismatched. DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED: rate limits, timeouts and maximum concurrency. Those are numeric limits with a unit and a direction, which is exactly what Constraint already carries (quantity/limit/direction) and budget_report already rolls up, and CONSTRAINS is already `*`→`*` so a Constraint can bind an Interface today — a second place to say the same number would drift from the first. That decision is pinned by its own test rather than left as a comment. Additive properties only, so the version stamp (which counts node and edge TYPES) does not move and older graphs stay readable.
properties.name: A published contract says what a consumer must agree with

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25. `Interface.designation` (internal | published, defaulting to internal because publishing is a commitment nobody should have asserted for them) plus `set_interface_designation`, plus the computation that earns the distinction: `propagate_from` now reports `boundary_crossings` — the published Interfaces a change passes through, NAMED rather than counted, in both the full radius and the summary, with `crosses_published_boundary` on each impacted node. That makes severability computed instead of asserted, which is what MOSA's Table D-1 asks a program to demonstrate and what an architecture diagram cannot prove: a change inside a part either crosses none of the design's published boundaries, or the report says which contract carried it and therefore whom to talk to. WHY THE DISTINCTION WAS WORTH ADDING: two independent routes arrived at the same missing property — MOSA's designation of modular system interfaces (from the guidebook Anthony supplied) and BL-45's system-of-systems thread, which recorded five days earlier that nothing marks an Interface external-facing. dec:edge-orthogonality's rule is satisfied because a computation reads it. FOUND BY A TEST, and it was a real bug: the first implementation counted a boundary ONE HOP PAST the depth bound as crossed, so an internal change reported crossing a contract the walk never reached. The crossing bookkeeping now sits after the depth guard, where a boundary beyond the bound belongs to truncated_beyond_depth instead. Also pinned: seeding a change ON a published interface is not a crossing (you are changing the promise, not passing through it — conflating them would make every ICD edit look like a containment failure), and withdrawing a designation removes the crossing, because the computation follows the design rather than remembering it. 8 tests. NOT DONE, and named rather than implied: no filtered export of "just the published surface" (req:design-composes needs it), and no per-module modularity view — the acquisition community's words for these criteria belong in a projection, never in the schema.
properties.name: Designate a published boundary, and compute whether a change stays behind it

properties.description: One command sets up or refreshes the design environment.
properties.name: Install into a consumer project

properties.description: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and COMPUTE when the design breaks one. BUILT 2026-07-25. Anthony's call on shape: a discriminated Constraint (`category: kpp`) rather than a new node type, because the quantity/limit/direction triple and the budget rollup are exactly what a KPP needs and already existed unused — and because an enum value plus a property is upgrade-SAFE where a new node type would refuse older binaries, which mattered on a day that already shipped two edge-type changes. Added `objective` beside the existing `limit`, giving the acquisition pair: threshold is the minimum acceptable, objective is what success looks like. Objective is optional and never invented, because a number the graph asserts on its own is the one thing intent vocabulary must not do. THREE VIOLATIONS, ranked ABOVE ordinary gaps because a breached KPP is not thinness in the design, it is the design failing. UNBOUND (0.90) — a KPP constraining nothing can never be violated, so it sits permanently green while asserting something vital; the quietest failure and the reason 'a KPP that nothing checks is a comment'. Reported once, not three times: an unbound KPP cannot also be breached or contradicted, and counting one fault three ways would teach people the findings are noise. BREACHED (0.95) — the budget rollup crossed the threshold, reusing budget_report wholesale. The only arithmetic violation, and the reason a KPP is worth distinguishing from a requirement nobody adds up. An INCOMPLETE rollup is deliberately NOT a breach: asserting failure from absent data is the silent guess this project forbids. CONTRADICTED (0.85) — an ACCEPTED decision governs what the KPP binds, surfaced for review and explicitly not asserted as a violation, since whether it truly costs the KPP is semantic. Proposed decisions are excluded: an open choice has traded nothing away, and flagging it would punish thinking out loud. 9 tests. FOUND WHILE BUILDING: GOVERNED_BY runs FROM the governed node TO the Decision, so the first implementation walked it backwards and found nothing — caught by the test rather than by review. THE CAPTURE HALF IS cap:kpp-proposal AND IS NOT BUILT: this computes violations of KPPs that exist; it does not notice that a stated need SHOULD be one.
properties.name: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and compute when the design breaks one

properties.description: The capture half of KPPs, and the half a person actually touches. BUILT 2026-07-25 as the kpp-proposal skill (art:kpp-proposal-skill) plus the typed write path it needs. Anthony, 2026-07-25: the user says "the system should be able to perform X"; the agent, acting as the systems-engineering SME the user is not required to be (req:no-se-knowledge), recognises the shape of inviolable intent and asks — that sounds like something that MUST be met, is it? — and the user confirms or declines. WHY THE AGENT MUST NOT DECIDE IT: criticality is a claim about consequence, not about wording. Whether missing a threshold FAILS THE EFFORT depends on mission, contract and money that the graph does not hold and the agent cannot see. An agent that promoted a requirement to KPP on its own would be asserting the user's stake in their own project, which is the same forgery dec:certainty-derived forbids for requirement status — and worse here, because a KPP outranks every ordinary gap and would drag the whole detector's ranking with it. So: the agent PROPOSES, the human DISPOSES, and nothing enters as a KPP without the user's word. WHAT THE AGENT CAN LEGITIMATELY NOTICE, and it is more than intuition. A statement carrying a unit-bearing threshold (500 miles, 3000 pounds, 500 milliseconds) is already shaped like a KPP and may simply be unmodelled — the quantity/limit/direction triple has somewhere to go. Language of necessity ('must', 'shall', 'no less than') against language of preference ('should', 'aims to') is a real signal in acquisition prose. And a requirement whose failure the user has elsewhere described as fatal is a candidate the graph itself can surface. THE QUESTION MUST CARRY THE CONSEQUENCE, not just the label: asking 'is this a KPP?' invites a shrug, whereas asking 'if the system missed this by ten percent, would the effort have failed?' is answerable by someone who has never heard the term — which is the test req:no-se-knowledge sets. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it was the reason this could not be skill-only: add_constraint had no `objective` parameter and its description never mentioned the kpp category, so the only way to record a confirmed KPP over MCP was the generic create_node — which is why the 9 tests of cap:kpp build their KPPs that way. A capture skill would have been pointing the agent at a door that was not there. add_constraint now takes objective and names the category, so what the user confirms is recordable through the typed helper (3 further tests). TWO GUARDS THE SKILL CARRIES that no test can enforce: it must not ask about every requirement (a design where everything is inviolable has no KPPs, and asking becomes noise the user waves through), and on a decline it records a small accepted Decision GOVERNED_BY the node, because the same signals will otherwise make it ask again next session — being asked the same question twice is how someone learns the tool is not listening. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT AUTOMATED: nothing scans the design for KPP candidates on its own. That would be a detector proposing the user's stakes to them, and the ask belongs where the words are still fresh — in the conversation that produced them.
properties.name: Notice when a stated need is really a KPP, and ask

properties.description: With `--only-if-present`, a session opened where no design has been started is served the LATENT surface: the handshake says reflow2 is installed and available and that this directory has no design, exactly one tool is served (`reflow2_start_design`), and NOTHING is created — no store, no state, no files. The check is a filesystem test on the graph's own directory, because opening is the thing that would create. Distinct from the degraded surface on purpose: degraded means a graph exists and could not be opened, which is an outage; latent means nobody ever made one, which is ordinary. The loop-nudge hook is gated by the same test, so a machine-wide hook registration is silent everywhere reflow2 is not being used.
properties.name: A directory with no design costs nothing

properties.description: One cheap call returning the coherence loop's outstanding debt as an ordered to-do list, computed from graph state alone.
properties.name: Say what the loop is owed

properties.description: Registers reflow2 with the user's agent at USER scope, so no project ever needs setting up: the MCP server (Claude Code via `claude mcp add -s user`, OpenCode via its user config), the ten slash commands into `~/.claude/commands/`, the coherence-loop hooks into `~/.claude/settings.json`, and a `reflow2` command on PATH whose subcommands are `install`, `init` and `check`. Idempotent and merge-only — it never overwrites a config it did not write, reports every file it left alone and why, has `--check` and `--uninstall`, and refuses to report success when a step failed. Run by `install.sh` automatically, so the release one-liner is the whole install for any user.
properties.name: Install reflow2 once for every project on a machine

properties.description: Every capability as a typed tool for an agent.
properties.name: Serve the loop over MCP

properties.description: Given a common-ancestor export and two divergent records, compute a typed three-way merge per node and per property (git's trivial-merge case table over typed values, not lines): where only one side changed, take it; where both changed differently, surface a structured conflict as a Question rather than guessing. Deletion is retain-and-ask. The write-side sibling of cap:compare-designs. BL-80 #1+#2, the core of BL-12's merge. BUILT + VERIFIED (art:merge, ver:merge, 46 tests): merge_designs proposes (writes nothing); resolve_merge materialises the merged design from the human's per-conflict decisions; apply_merge commits it into the live graph atomically, refusing until every conflict is decided. Surfaces: merge_designs (read-only) + apply_merge (write) MCP tools; and the file-pure git-file pair of CLI modes --merge (propose, printing conflicts and their ids) and --merge-apply (apply a decisions file with resolve_merge, printing the merged export document, never touching the graph and refusing until every conflict is decided). Base is git's merge-base; the reflow2-native DAG is BL-70; rerere is BL-80 #5.
properties.name: Three-way merge two divergent designs

properties.description: Record how a human resolved a merge conflict — content-keyed (property + base/ours/theirs values, node-independent) — and offer it back when the same conflict recurs. Stored in the graph as an answered Question whose id IS the content key (rr: prefix; the Question schema has no source field, so the prefix distinguishes it and it stays invisible to open_questions). Advisory: recall_resolutions surfaces the recorded choice; the human confirms, or bulk-accepts via apply_merge use_recorded. BUILT + VERIFIED (art:merge, ver:merge): resolution_key on each property/edge-property conflict, record on apply, recall_resolutions tool. Extends cap:merge-designs; BL-80 #5. v1 covers property + edge-property conflicts (node-type/delete-modify keys deferred).
properties.name: Reuse a recorded conflict resolution (rerere)

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25, the first rung of dec:nested-graphs option (c). An edge cannot cross a store because the schema validates both endpoints, so designs link by MIRRORING: `mirror_surface` brings another design's published surface in as local nodes marked `provenance: imported`, and the mirrored Project carries the coordinate — `mirror_of` (whose design), `mirror_content_hash` (which version of their surface), `mirrored_at` (when). Afterwards your own components provides/consumes the mirrored Interface with ORDINARY LOCAL EDGES, so the golden thread, propagate, and every detector work unchanged: foreignness became a property of the NODE rather than of the link, which is what makes the whole approach cheap. `mirrors()` lists who you are composed with and at what version. THE GUARD THAT MATTERS: import_graph is an upsert, so mirroring a surface whose ids collide with local ones would silently overwrite your design with someone else's nodes. A collision is REPORTED AND SKIPPED — your node survives untouched, and an edge touching a collided id is dropped rather than rewired, because pointing their PROVIDES at your same-named component would fabricate a relationship neither design asserted (dec:ask-not-repair). Two designs using one id for different things is a naming conversation between owners, not a merge. Mirroring a design into itself is refused outright, naming import_graph as what you meant. WHAT THE BUILD EXPOSED, and it is the honest limit: every reflow2 graph carried the same hardcoded graph_id, so no design could tell another from itself — rule:no-foreclosure item 5 arriving as a concrete blocker rather than a hypothetical. `open_in_memory_as` lets a design name itself, which is enough for library use and for the tests, but a DURABLE design's identity has to be remembered beside the store (the id namespaces every key, so reopening under a different name would find nothing). That is req:design-identity, filed rather than half-built. 7 tests, including the seam one: after mirroring, consuming their contract reports a published-boundary crossing — which is exactly what changing your side of somebody else's interface is.
properties.name: Compose two designs by mirroring the other's published surface, coordinate and all

properties.description: Anthony, 2026-07-25: "you have requirements A and C, but you missed B." A genuinely different kind of gap from everything detect_gaps finds today. Every existing gap source reasons about STRUCTURE — this requirement has no capability, this capability has no check — and each is deterministic because the hole is visible in the graph's shape. A missing requirement is invisible in the shape: the design is perfectly coherent without it, which is exactly why nobody notices. TWO AXES, and the user's fighter-jet example shows they are different detections. BREADTH is the bigger one: a stakeholder states that the wings must provide X lift and sustain Y G, and the engine must make Z thrust — two SUBSYSTEM-level requirements, which implies a subsystem decomposition in which landing gear, avionics, fuel, flight controls, life support, structures, hydraulics and thermal have nothing whatsoever. That is not interpolating a missing item between two others; it is noticing that 2 of roughly 12 expected subsystems have been named at all, which requires knowing what kind of thing is being built. DEPTH is the second: the wing requirement is itself thin, since wings need more than lift and G-load. Both are semantic — pattern-matching against a domain archetype — so they belong to the LLM half of dec:three-party-checks, not the deterministic core. Bounded accordingly: the agent proposes, the graph records at `proposed`, the human decides, and nothing enters above proposed, or the tool starts inventing intent and dec:human-decides is broken in the way that matters most. cap:requirement-lineage sharpens it considerably — requirement families (which Leiden already clusters, once requirement-to-requirement edges exist) are precisely where an omission is both most likely and most detectable, because a family with two members in a design whose siblings have twenty is visible without knowing any domain at all. PLANNED.
properties.name: Notice the requirement nobody wrote down

properties.description: Represent an ordered flow of activities with roles on its edges.
properties.name: Model a process, not only a product

properties.description: A first baseline and a clean check are recorded as what they are, rather than as changes that never happened. `set_artifact_checksum` gains a third disposition, `baseline_established`, for an artifact registered with no checksum getting its first one — the record moves and the code does not — and which disposition is available is a fact about the artifact rather than a preference: an accept against no baseline is refused, and a baseline_established that would MOVE an existing one is refused, so the new word cannot launder real drift past the two-sided accept. A recording reconcile stamps `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` on every artifact observed to still match, so a pass that found everything correct is distinguishable from a pass nobody ran; the confirmation ledger counts those toward examined, and reports first baselines apart from accepts because a first baseline is not a judgement anyone made.
properties.name: The ledger can say that nothing moved

properties.description: Two halves. PROOF: tools/test_nudge_path.py reads .claude/settings.json, takes the command the harness would run, and runs THAT with the JSON a real Stop hook receives — asserting the {"decision":"block"} the harness actually consumes, that the reason names what happened, that a session which ran the loop check is left alone, and that the nudge fires once (on the harness's stop_hook_active) rather than holding a session hostage. BACKSTOP: the server looks for a registered Stop hook and reports installed | absent | broken (registered but the script is missing — the dangerous middle case, since the settings file looks right) | unknown (project dir undeterminable, never reported as absent). The advisory rides the HANDSHAKE INSTRUCTIONS, the one channel every session reads unasked, and loop_status carries the same as a machine-readable field. This matters because reflow2_init installs no hooks at all: every consumer project has no session-end nudge, and until now nothing said so.
properties.name: The loop's own safety net is checked, and its absence is announced

properties.description: Answer "we need to add this — where does it go?" from the graph, for someone who did not build the system. Assembles machinery that already exists and has never been pointed at this question: map the newcomer's words onto the parts that exist, show what touching each candidate would reach, name the decisions already governing that area and who authored them, name the intent it must not break, and say honestly which parts of the real system the design does not cover. Distinct from saying where the design stands, which answers what the system is and what was decided but not where new work belongs. No core change — a skill over existing operations. PLANNED — BL-101.
properties.name: Tell a newcomer where a new piece of work belongs

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the parallel-work skill — the procedure that ties the pieces together, chosen over the three alternatives in dec:concurrent-work-isolation because it needed no new architecture: a git worktree already gives each person a separate checkout, the graph store is single-writer PER DIRECTORY so each worktree can run its own server, and cap:git-merge-driver now merges the design semantically on the way back. Claim the region (advisory, never a lock), work isolated, export before every commit that touched the design, let the driver merge, release the claim, reconcile. WHAT THE SKILL IS REQUIRED TO SAY OUT LOUD, because these are the things people assume are handled: a claim is invisible to the other person until they pull, and nothing refuses a write; the design merges semantically but the CODE beside it merges exactly as before, so two people can hold disjoint design regions and still collide in the same module; and `--ours`/`--theirs` on a design conflict discards a node someone wrote, with nothing to tell you afterwards. This is parallel work with good merges, not simultaneous editing — the live-collaboration road stays open in dec:central-host with its counter-argument recorded.
properties.name: Two people work one design at once through isolation, not through a lock

properties.description:
When a planned epoch's content changes — a requirement moves out of epoch 5, a date slips — the movement itself is recorded and dated, rather than the plan being silently rewritten to look as though it always said the new thing. The forward-looking sibling of the snapshot machinery the backward axis already has.

THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTION IS ANSWERED (2026-07-31, by measurement rather than choice): filing in the arrived epoch IS sufficient, and planned epochs need no revision chain of their own. `record_change`'s planned-epoch refusal keys on the epoch you FILE INTO, not the node you snapshot, so a replan is recorded in the current arrived epoch with the planned epoch as its SUBJECT — and because a snapshot captures incoming edges, snapshotting that epoch captures the entire plan pointed at it in one call.

BUILT as the `SCHEDULED_FOR` guard: removing, re-pointing or rewriting the modality of a schedule edge is REFUSED while the plan is unrecorded, so the movement cannot fail to be dated.
